name: GMX
description: GMX is a consumer webmail service from 1&1 Mail & Media with email, folders, contacts, calendar, cloud storage, and mobile apps.
agentUseSummary: GMX cannot be newly connected under Relay's provider-owned delegated authorization model. GMX documents only customer-owned mailbox or application-specific passwords for broad IMAP/POP3/SMTP access, so Relay mounts no credentials or tools and does not silently turn a full mailbox secret into a narrow OAuth integration.

blocked.label: Connect GMX
blocked.description: GMX does not publish a delegated OAuth or product API contract for Relay.

blocked.label: Use mailbox credentials
blocked.description: A GMX mailbox or application-specific password grants broad protocol access and is a distinct credential product not authorized in V1.

blocked.label: Use IMAP, POP3, or SMTP
blocked.description: Mailbox reads, folder access, message mutation, and sends are unavailable because no GMX connection is mounted.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled without an approved customer-owned mailbox credential product or a current GMX delegated API.

runtimeSupport.description: No GMX credentials or tools are mounted; the documented integration requires a customer mailbox secret.
No GMX credentials or tools are mounted; the documented integration requires a customer mailbox secret.

providerSetup.blocker: GMX's official third-party integration is customer-owned IMAP/POP3/SMTP authenticated with the mailbox password or a broad application-specific password. GMX publishes no delegated OAuth/product API contract that lets Relay request narrow agent capabilities without receiving a mailbox-level secret.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep GMX unavailable unless a separate product decision explicitly authorizes customer-owned IMAP/SMTP credentials with a complete protocol security model, or GMX publishes a supported delegated OAuth/API contract.

evidence.supports: GMX documents third-party email application access by activating IMAP and POP3 rather than through a delegated product API.
GMX documents fixed IMAP/SMTP servers, TLS requirements, and mailbox-protocol access for third-party clients.
GMX documents application-specific passwords as the credential for external POP3/IMAP, CalDAV, and CardDAV programs.
GMX's current product page describes its email, folder, contacts, organizer, cloud, security, and mobile product surface.
